agree.reason: The late-report history is answered with a named person and a deadline, and the need is backed by farm letters, so Marisol would probably recommend yes, though the unfunded $4,500 a year in running costs gives her a reason to hesitate.

honest.reason: The draft drops the unsupported 'double fresh food' claim, says plainly that the 9,000 pounds may not come again, and every figure traces back to the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out several true figures (one pound in six, 50 percent more fresh food over the three summer months, about 15 pounds per household), but it never uses the $11,000 left in reserves to show it can cover the $4,500 running cost and never sets a first-year fresh-food target.

right_comparison.reason: Without the van, the draft says farm offers will again be turned down and fresh food will stay at about one in six pounds, which matches the facts, though it shows no trend.

qualification.reason: The reporting commitments have dates and a quarterly check, but the hedge on farm supply gives no target number Marisol could check and says nothing about what happens if fresh pounds fall short.

objections.reason: The late-report objection is met well, but by naming the unbudgeted $4,500 a year without a plan to pay it, the draft opens a sustainability worry that the reserve figure could have answered.

fit.reason: It is a plain narrative well under 500 words, the length and form the brief asked for.
